biography: Juarez Soares hails from the sun-drenched streets of Rio de Janeiro, a city where the roar of engines is as familiar as the samba beat. Unlike many who climb the motorsport ladder through karting academies, Juarez's entry was far more grassroots. He spent his teenage years tearing around makeshift dirt tracks in a beat-up go-kart his father, a retired mechanic, had cobbled together. His raw talent was undeniable, catching the eye of a local racing enthusiast who sponsored him into regional karting events. Early success led to a move into Formula Vee, where his aggressive, sometimes reckless, style both thrilled and frustrated team managers. After a stint in Formula 3 Sudamericana, Juarez found a home with MetalMoro, piloting their MRX Honda P3 prototype. His career is still on the ascent, marked by flashes of brilliance interspersed with costly errors – a reflection of his inconsistent temperament. A particularly memorable moment was at Interlagos in 2022, where he recovered from a spin on the first lap to finish second, showcasing his undeniable speed and tenacity.
drivingStyle: Juarez is known for his aggressive, attacking style. He's a late-braker, often pushing the limits of grip to gain an advantage in corners. While this approach can lead to spectacular overtakes, it also makes him prone to errors, particularly in wet conditions. Tire management is an area where he struggles, often burning through his rubber early in a stint. Under pressure, Juarez tends to become even more aggressive, sometimes leading to ill-advised moves and contact with other drivers.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from their Formula Vee days, fueled by constant on-track battles and accusations of unfair tactics.
A more recent rivalry that ignited when Isabela publicly criticized Juarez's driving style after a collision at Goiânia, calling him 'reckless and dangerous'.
A clash of egos. Both drivers see themselves as the future of Brazilian motorsport and constantly try to outdo each other both on and off the track.

quirks: Always wears the same faded Senna t-shirt under his racing suit.
Listens to a specific playlist of Brazilian funk music before every race.
Has a habit of talking to his car, especially when he's struggling with setup.
famousQuote: "You don't win races by being polite. Sometimes you gotta send it!"
careerHighlight: Finishing second at the Interlagos round of the Brazilian Endurance Championship in 2022, after starting from the back of the grid due to a qualifying penalty. He overtook six cars in the final ten laps.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the 2023 6 Hours of Curitiba after a misjudgment in wet conditions, costing his team a potential victory and valuable championship points.
